metadata.title: The Assessment Frameworks for Cycle 2 of PIAAC

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is an assessment-framework chapter for PIAAC Cycle 2 rather than an empirical analysis of microdata. It describes how the numeracy and adaptive problem solving constructs are operationalised through item design, task dimensions, scoring rules, and planned administration (e.g., tablet-based delivery, adaptive testing, field trial and main study). Because no student-level dataset is analysed here, the paper does not report the use of complex survey weights or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) for estimation. For analysts using PIAAC microdata in later empirical work, weighting and replicate design should follow the official PIAAC technical documentation for the relevant cycle; this framework chapter itself does not specify weight variable names or replication methods.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a framework and construct/assessment-design document that does not estimate cognitive achievement scores using plausible values (PVs) at the student level. The text focuses on defining dimensions (e.g., numeracy cognitive processes, content, representations, context) and on how tasks/items will be built, trialled, and scored (often dichotomously) rather than on producing PV-based outcome models. Missing-data handling is therefore not applicable in the sense of an empirical modelling strategy, because no analytic dataset with missingness is analysed in this chapter.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic sample is defined because the document is a conceptual/assessment-framework chapter. It describes planned field trial and main study procedures (e.g., tablet-based administration, adaptive design, item pool blueprinting) but does not report an empirical dataset or inclusion/exclusion criteria for an analysed sample.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Skills Studies framework chapter defines how PIAAC Cycle 2 will assess adult numeracy and adaptive problem solving (APS) through updated construct models and item/task specifications. For numeracy, it specifies four core dimensions—cognitive processes, content, representations, and context—and explains how these dimensions guide item development, including the move from a prior “response” facet to a richer cognitive-process description aligned with PISA processes. For APS, it defines APS as goal-directed problem solving in dynamic situations requiring cognitive and metacognitive processes, and it specifies task dimensions (problem configuration, dynamics, environment features, information environment, and context) that drive item difficulty. The chapter also outlines planned administration features (tablet delivery, adaptive testing, locator test pathways), scoring principles (often dichotomous with partial credit only when construct-relevant), and the role of field trials and quality assurance for validity and fairness. No empirical model results are reported because the document is not an analysis of PIAAC microdata.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is intentionally sparse because the provided text is an OECD assessment-framework document rather than an empirical study. It does not report an analysed student sample, PV estimation, missing-data strategy, or any ML model training/evaluation. Consequently, fields that require empirical outcomes (e.g., main_findings with performance metrics) are left empty by design.
